column2: Computer scientist who in 1994 devised Simon's algorithm, the first to show an exponential quantum speedup over classical probabilistic algorithms. It directly inspired Shor's factoring algorithm.
Computer scientist who with Umesh Vazirani wrote a foundational 1993 paper on quantum complexity theory, defining the class BQP and giving the Bernstein–Vazirani algorithm.
Computer scientist who in 1996, at Bell Labs, discovered Grover's search algorithm, which finds an item among N in about √N steps.
Mathematician who in 1994 found Shor's algorithm for factoring and discrete logarithms, and in 1995 the first quantum error-correcting code. He is a professor at MIT.
Mathematical physicist, co-author of the Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm (1992) and of the 1993 paper that proposed quantum teleportation.
Computer scientist at UC Berkeley, a founder of quantum complexity theory (with Ethan Bernstein) and a pioneer of device-independent cryptography and certified randomness.
Physicist at MIT, co-author of the HHL algorithm for linear systems of equations, with work spanning quantum algorithms and information theory.
Physicist at MIT who co-invented adiabatic quantum computation and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA).
Computer scientist known for quantum complexity theory, including boson sampling (with Alex Arkhipov), and for explaining quantum computing on his blog Shtetl-Optimized.
Physicist who invented the toric code and topological quantum computation, and showed the local Hamiltonian problem is QMA-complete. The Solovay–Kitaev theorem also bears his name.
Physicist at the University of Oxford who invented the seven-qubit Steane code (1996) and co-developed CSS codes.
Physicist who developed the stabilizer formalism, the Gottesman–Knill theorem and, with Kitaev and Preskill, the GKP bosonic code.
Physicist at NIST who co-developed the Knill–Laflamme error-correction conditions, the KLM protocol for optical quantum computing, and methods for benchmarking gates.
Physicist at Caltech who coined the terms "quantum supremacy" (2012) and "NISQ" (2018), and is a leading researcher in fault-tolerant quantum computing.
Physicist, founding director of the Institute for Quantum Computing at the University of Waterloo, co-author of the Knill–Laflamme conditions and the KLM protocol.
French physicist whose 1982 experiments tested Bell inequalities with entangled photons, closing important loopholes. He shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Austrian physicist who led the first quantum teleportation experiment (1997) and many entanglement experiments. The GHZ state is partly named after him; he shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics.
American physicist who performed the first experimental Bell test in 1972 and co-authored the CHSH inequality. He shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Northern Irish physicist who proved Bell's theorem in 1964, showing that no local hidden-variable theory can reproduce quantum mechanics.
Physicist at the University of Oxford who in 1985 defined the universal quantum computer and gave the first quantum algorithm, founding the theory of quantum computation.
Physicist at Argonne National Laboratory who in 1980 described a quantum mechanical model of a Turing machine, one of the first steps toward quantum computers.
Nobel-winning physicist who in 1981 argued that simulating quantum physics needs a computer built on quantum mechanics, an idea that launched the field.
Russian mathematician who suggested the idea of quantum computing in 1980, noting that quantum systems may be too complex to simulate classically.
Physicist at the University of Basel who with David DiVincenzo proposed in 1998 using electron spins in quantum dots as qubits, the basis of spin-qubit hardware.
Physicist known for the DiVincenzo criteria (2000), the list of requirements for building a quantum computer, and for the Loss–DiVincenzo spin-qubit proposal.
Physicist at NIST whose trapped-ion experiments achieved precise control of single quantum systems, including early quantum logic gates. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Physicist at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics who with Peter Zoller proposed in 1995 how to build a quantum computer with trapped ions.
Physicist who led Google's quantum hardware team for its 2019 quantum supremacy experiment. He shared the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
Austrian physicist at the University of Innsbruck who with Ignacio Cirac proposed the trapped-ion quantum computer in 1995, and pioneered quantum simulation with cold atoms.
French physicist whose cavity experiments trapped photons and observed quantum states and decoherence in action. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physics with David Wineland.
Russian mathematician who proved the Holevo bound in 1973, limiting how much classical information quantum states can carry.
Physicist who proposed the E91 protocol in 1991, basing quantum key distribution on entanglement and Bell inequalities.
Physicist at IBM who co-invented BB84 quantum key distribution and quantum teleportation, and pioneered reversible computation.
Computer scientist at the Université de Montréal who co-invented BB84 quantum key distribution with Charles Bennett, and co-authored quantum teleportation.
Physicist at MIT who showed in 1996 that quantum computers can efficiently simulate local quantum systems, and co-authored the HHL algorithm.
